methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $300K total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Hedral is a seed-stage company in Housing & Construction founded by Arjo Mozumder, having raised $0.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of five private peers in the same sector (BotBuilt, Apis Cor, Unlimited Industries, Ground Control Development, and ADMARES), with no public comparables available for direct benchmarking.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach given data availability. Using the $300K total raised as a proxy baseline valuation and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to model progression from Seed to the next financing stage, this method implies a valuation of $750K. This reflects the expectation that the company will execute on its current plan and advance to Series A, though without additional methodologies (revenue multiples, DCF, or cross-sectional comp analysis), the analysis rests on a single method.

The triangulated range spans $638K to $862K, with a median of $750K. This narrow band reflects limited data inputs rather than high conviction; the analysis is materially constrained by the absence of public comparables and limited disclosure from private peers. Key uncertainties include the company's current burn rate, path to revenue, and relative competitive positioning within the construction-tech subsector. Further diligence on peer-company metrics would be required to validate or adjust this range.
